title: The Uneven Impact of Generative AI on Entrepreneurial Performance: Evidence from a Field Experiment in Kenya
extended_summary:
This paper asks whether a GPT-4-powered generative AI business assistant can improve the performance of small business entrepreneurs, and whether its effects differ across entrepreneurs with different baseline performance levels. The motivation is that AI may help people make better decisions, but it is unclear whether such benefits extend to the open-ended, messy tasks involved in running a real business.

The authors ran a field experiment with 640 Kenyan small business entrepreneurs. Participants were randomly assigned either to receive access to a WhatsApp-based AI business assistant or to a placebo control condition consisting of static business training guides delivered through WhatsApp. The assistant provided context-specific advice, allowed follow-up questions, and was designed to help entrepreneurs with a wide range of business decisions. Outcomes were measured with repeated self-reported surveys of profit and revenue, combined into a standardized business performance index.

The study finds no statistically significant average effect of AI access on business performance overall. However, there is strong heterogeneity by baseline performance: entrepreneurs who were initially lower-performing did worse with the AI assistant, while initially higher-performing entrepreneurs may have benefited. The authors conclude that generative AI can influence real-world business outcomes, but the benefits are uneven and depend on users’ judgment in selecting and implementing advice. The paper further suggests that simply providing AI access is not enough; user capability and context are crucial to whether AI improves performance.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a field randomized controlled trial with a clearly defined treatment and control condition, stratified randomization, and multiple robustness checks. Credibility is strong, though the setting is not K-12 and the outcome is not directly educational, so relevance to the target taxonomy is limited.
impact_tier_rationale: The average effect is essentially null (0.04 sd, not significant), and the negative effect for low performers offsets the positive effect for high performers. Because the paper reports heterogeneous business-performance impacts rather than a clear positive improvement for the general population, the overall impact is unclear to modest at best.

interventions.use_case: GPT-4-powered WhatsApp business assistant that provides context-specific entrepreneurial advice in an interactive chat format, with follow-up questions and enumerated recommendations for Kenyan small business owners.

finding.finding_summary: The paper evaluates whether access to a GPT-4-based AI business assistant improved small business performance in Kenya. The average treatment effect on the standardized business performance index was small and not statistically significant (β=0.04 sd, p=0.34, 95% CI [-0.05, 0.15]) in a sample of n=640 entrepreneurs, but effects varied sharply by baseline performance.
finding.measure: Standardized business performance index combining self-reported weekly and monthly profits and revenues
finding.effect_size: 0.04 sd (overall); -0.08 sd for low performers; 0.16 sd for high performers; heterogeneity = 0.23 sd
finding.confidence_interval: overall 95% CI [-0.05, 0.15]; low performers [-0.13, -0.03]; high performers [-0.02, 0.33]; heterogeneity [-0.41, -0.05]
finding.std_deviation: Outcome standardized using the control group post-treatment SD
